annotations.text:
(Recommended) Dial A · axis: card tone.
Why: this is the shipped .tdial geometry on /timneh-african-grey-for-sale/ and /congo-african-grey-for-sale/ (196px card, 64px ring, .74rem rows, always-visible tag pill), so it is measured rather than proposed, and its numerals #6b625a on white read 5.9:1, the highest of the three. The 2026-07-23 density pass that shrank these rows to .7rem with the tag hidden was rejected by the breeder in one line: I can hardly read the text or click.
Trade-off: a near-white card on a cream page has the least separation from the body, so it leans entirely on the 1px border and the warm shadow to read as an object.

Dial B · axis: card tone.
Why: numerals #9fc7b0 on aviary #234f3b measure 5.0:1 and the dark block separates from the cream page without needing a border, which is why the hand-raised page ships it. Geometry is untouched; only the palette moves.
Trade-off: a dark 594px block in the left gutter competes with the hero and the footer for weight, and the two contrast pairs must never be crossed. The light card's #6b625a on #234f3b is unreadable. The active row sits on a lighter #2e5c48 tint where #9fc7b0 falls to 4.11:1, so the active numeral is #c3ded0 (5.36:1); that third pair is part of the variation.
Open question (critique pass): the tag pill reproduces the shipped .tdial .tag exactly, a clay-ink fill with white text, but at eighteen rows the tag column carries more visual weight than the labels it annotates. Retinting the tag on the dark card would read better and would diverge from the component that ships.

Dial C · axis: grouping.
Why: the homepage rail carries 18 sections under four named parts. Ungrouped, rows 07 to 18 read as one undifferentiated block, the same failure the mobile bottom sheet already solved by naming the parts.
Trade-off: four part headers add 91px to the card (685px against 594px) and duplicate the part signal already carried by the always-visible tag pill.
